title: Shiny Live Applications
text:
Shiny Live (often referred to as Shinylive) is an approach that allows Shiny applications to run directly in a web browser without requiring a dedicated server.
Unlike traditional Shiny apps, which rely on a server to process data and return results, Shiny Live runs everything on the client side. This makes it easier to share and deploy interactive applications.

Shiny Live (often referred to as Shinylive) is an approach that allows Shiny applications to run directly in a web browser without requiring a dedicated server.
Unlike traditional Shiny apps, which rely on a server to process data and return results, Shiny Live runs everything on the client side. This makes it easier to share and deploy interactive applications.

title: Shiny Live Applications
text:
How Shiny Live Works
Shiny Live uses modern web technologies to bring Shiny apps into the browser:

Applications are converted into static web files (HTML, CSS, and JavaScript)

R code runs in the browser using WebAssembly through tools like webR

The browser acts as both the client and the server

This means that once deployed, the app does not need a running R server to function. :contentReferenceoaicite:0

title: Shiny Live Applications
text:
Key Features

Runs entirely in the browser

No need for server hosting

Easy deployment on platforms like GitHub Pages

Maintains interactivity similar to traditional Shiny apps

title: Shiny Live Applications
text:
Why Use Shiny Live?
Shiny Live simplifies the process of sharing interactive applications. Since it does not require server infrastructure, it reduces hosting costs and setup complexity.
It is especially useful for: - Demonstrations
- Teaching materials
- Lightweight dashboards
- Public data exploration tools
Because everything runs locally in the user’s browser, applications can be distributed as static websites. :contentReferenceoaicite:1

title: Shiny Live Applications
text:
Integration with Quarto
Shiny Live integrates well with Quarto, allowing developers to embed interactive applications directly into web pages and presentations.
Using the Shinylive extension, you can include live Shiny apps inside .qmd files, making your website both informative and interactive. :contentReferenceoaicite:2

title: Shiny Live Applications
text:
Limitations
While Shiny Live is powerful, it has some limitations:

Performance depends on the user’s device

Large or complex computations may be slower

Initial load time may be longer due to downloading required resources

title: Shiny Live Applications
text:
Conclusion
Shiny Live provides a modern way to deploy Shiny applications without relying on servers. It makes interactive data tools more accessible, easier to share, and simpler to host, especially for lightweight applications and educational content.

title: Shiny Applications
text:
Shiny is an R package used to build interactive web applications and dashboards. It allows users to turn data analysis into web-based tools that can be accessed through a browser, without requiring advanced web development skills.
This makes it especially useful for sharing insights with others in a simple and interactive way.

title: Shiny Applications
text:
How Shiny Works
A typical Shiny application has two main parts:

User Interface (UI)
The user interface controls what appears on the screen. This includes elements such as buttons, sliders, input boxes, and visual outputs like charts and tables.


Server
The server is responsible for the behind-the-scenes work. It processes user inputs, performs calculations, and updates outputs accordingly.
Shiny uses a reactive approach, meaning that outputs automatically update whenever a user changes an input.

title: Shiny Applications
text:
Key Features

Interactive data visualizations

Real-time updates based on user input

Seamless integration with R

No need for extensive knowledge of HTML, CSS, or JavaScript

title: Shiny Applications
text:
Why Use Shiny?
Shiny is widely used in data science and research because it simplifies the process of sharing data insights. Instead of presenting static reports, users can explore data themselves through interactive dashboards.
It is particularly helpful when working with complex datasets that benefit from user-driven exploration.

title: Shiny Applications
text:
Common Use Cases

Dashboards for data analysis

Tools for exploring research data

Reporting and decision-support systems

Teaching and learning applications

title: Shiny Applications
text:
Conclusion
Shiny provides a practical way to build interactive applications directly from R. It helps make data more accessible and easier to understand, especially for users without a technical background.
